title: The Story of Philosophy: The Lives and Opinions of the World’s Greatest Philosophers
author: Will Durant
target_audience: Those seeking an accessible introduction to Western philosophy
core_themes: The evolution and development of Western philosophy
Major ideas and arguments of prominent philosophers
Interconnectedness of philosophical movements over time
Practical relevance of philosophy to modern life
primary_purpose: To introduce and explain the lives, historical context, and major ideas of the world’s most influential Western philosophers in an accessible, engaging narrative that makes philosophy approachable to laypeople.

structure_format.narrative_style: Engaging, narrative-driven, integrative and often anecdotal
structure_format.organization: Chronological exploration, with each chapter focused on one or more key philosophers and their contributions
features: Summaries of key philosophical arguments and works

key_concepts_lessons: Philosophy is deeply rooted in the lives and times of its practitioners.
Recurring questions about existence, knowledge, ethics, and meaning drive philosophical inquiry.
Each major philosopher both inherits and challenges the ideas of predecessors.
Philosophy permeates science, politics, art, and daily living.
Understanding philosophical history grants perspective on the development of modern thought.
notable_features: Blends biography with exposition of philosophical ideas
Written for lay audiences without presuming specialized background
One of the earliest popularizations of philosophy in the 20th century
Includes analysis of primary works and doctrines
cultural_historical_context: Written in the 1920s, a period when educational resources on philosophy for the public were rare, Durant’s book helped spark wider interest in the humanities. It reflected a movement to democratize knowledge following World War I, and it shaped American engagement with Western intellectual traditions through much of the 20th century.
reception_impact: Bestseller upon release, with continued popularity over decades
Credited with inspiring countless readers to further study philosophy
Praised for readability and lively storytelling
Some academic critics note occasional simplification or interpretive bias
Influential in broadening the audience for philosophical writing
comparable_titles: A History of Western Philosophy by Bertrand Russell
The Philosophy Book (DK’s Big Ideas Simply Explained series)
The Problems of Philosophy by Bertrand Russell
